_comment: Nearshore forecast points for the Algerian Mediterranean coast. Each point is moved 3-6 km offshore of the city so the marine model returns sea-state rather than nulls or land-contaminated values. 'exposure' records which swell directions reach the site unobstructed - it is the single biggest reason two points 10 km apart can behave completely differently. THESE ARE DESK ESTIMATES: before relying on them, review each against the actual beach, marina and bay with someone who sails there.

exposure.sheltered_from: W and SW swell (Cap Caxine headland)
exposure.notes: Bay of Algiers opens NE. The commercial port and Sidi Fredj marina are far better sheltered than the open beaches east of the bay.
Gulf of Oran opens N/NW. Strong exposure to NW swell; Mers el-Kebir is markedly more sheltered than the eastern gulf.

exposure.sheltered_from: W and NW swell (Cap Carbon / Mont Gouraya)
exposure.notes: The bay opens E/SE. Cap Carbon blocks the dominant NW swell, so Bejaia is often workable when Algiers is not. claude.md listed 36.7525 here, identical to the Algiers latitude - corrected.
Gulf of Annaba opens N/NE, bounded W by Cap de Garde. Long fetch to the NE.
Straight, north-facing coast with little natural shelter outside the port. Fully exposed to N and NW swell.
Eastern side of the Gulf of Arzew, north-facing. Exposed to NW swell wrapping into the gulf.
